questions.q: How does the summary characterise Sancho Panza's part in the story?
a: An opportunist who was also a good friend
A coward who abandons the quest
A rival knight travelling in disguise
A wealthy noble with no interest in rewards
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Sancho seized the chance for reward but stayed loyal, helping Quixote through every challenge.

questions.q: What did Quixote believe the inn was on the night of his first challenge?
a: A castle where he could be knighted
A prison holding his lady
A church run by friars
A fortress full of enemies
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Quixote's delusion first showed when he took the inn for a castle and asked the innkeeper to knight him.

questions.q: What did Quixote mistake the windmills for?
a: Giants he had to fight
Castles full of nobles
Armies of the wicked
Dragons guarding treasure
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the famous episode where Quixote charges more than thirty windmills as if they were giants.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the stories we tell ourselves?
a: They comfort us now but distort reality over time
They are harmless unless we act on them
They always reflect the world more clearly
They help others understand us better
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues Quixote's invented world felt good immediately but left him isolated and disappointed later.

questions.q: What does the bond between Quixote and Sancho illustrate?
a: Everyone needs someone to share their troubles with
Loyalty must be bought with a reward
Friends should correct each other's delusions
Adventure is better undertaken alone
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the pair shows that every person needs a soul to share challenges with, like a knight needs a squire.
